title: Tata Steel Q2 Profit Rises 16% to Rs 3,700 Crore on India Strength
excerpt: Consolidated reported profit after tax rose 16.2% to Rs 3,699.59 crore in the September quarter as revenue from operations climbed 11.5% to Rs 65,436.24 crore and EBITDA reached Rs 10,665 crore.
body:
• Tata Steel's consolidated reported profit after tax for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 rose 16.2% year on year to Rs 3,699.59 crore, on revenue from operations up 11.5% to Rs 65,436.24 crore.
  • Consolidated EBITDA rose 17% year on year to Rs 10,665 crore, with India revenue of Rs 42,653 crore and India EBITDA of Rs 10,634 crore at a margin of about 25%.
  • On a different basis — profit attributable to owners — BusinessLine reported net profit up 18% at Rs 3,660 crore against Rs 3,102 crore a year earlier; that attributable figure is not the same as the Rs 3,700 crore total reported profit, and the two should not be mixed.
  • Noel Naval Tata will retire as non-executive, non-independent director and vice chairman at the close of business on November 11, 2026, according to the company's disclosure reported by BusinessLine and other coverage.

Tata Steel reported consolidated profit after tax of Rs 3,699.59 crore for the second quarter of FY27, the quarter ended September 30, 2026, up 16.2% from Rs 3,183.09 crore a year earlier. Revenue from operations rose 11.5% to Rs 65,436.24 crore from Rs 58,689.29 crore, supported by stronger Indian volumes and improved operating performance in the Netherlands.

Consolidated EBITDA stood at Rs 10,665 crore, up 17% from a year earlier and 14% from the previous quarter, with an EBITDA margin of around 16%. The reported profit included a net exceptional gain of about Rs 349 crore in the quarter, according to coverage of the company's release — a detail readers should keep separate from the underlying operating performance.

Two profit figures, two bases

Coverage of the same results also carries a second profit number, and it measures something different. BusinessLine reported that net profit attributable to owners rose 18% to Rs 3,660 crore, against Rs 3,102 crore in the same period last year, on the back of better realisation. Reported consolidated profit after tax — the Rs 3,699.59 crore figure in the lead — is the group's total profit; profit attributable to owners excludes the portion belonging to non-controlling interests. Both can be correct at once because they are different bases.

BusinessLine put revenue on its reporting basis at Rs 64,974 crore, up 12% from Rs 58,216 crore, and EBITDA at Rs 10,665 crore, up from Rs 9,106 crore, with EBITDA per tonne at Rs 13,462. The EBITDA total agrees across the coverage; the revenue line differs from the Rs 65,436.24 crore revenue-from-operations figure reported in the company's consolidated results summary, so this article keeps the two revenue figures labelled by source rather than blending them.

India carried the quarter

India remained the strongest operating market. India revenue stood at Rs 42,653 crore, while India EBITDA reached Rs 10,634 crore, giving an EBITDA margin of 25%. Crude steel production in India rose 7% quarter on quarter to 6.18 million tonnes, and deliveries rose 16% to 5.98 million tonnes.

Chief executive and managing director T V Narendran said the company was making progress on its volume and value growth agenda in India, supported by customer engagement and a resilient supply chain. BusinessLine quoted Narendran as saying that, despite ongoing geoeconomic uncertainty and higher raw material costs, the company delivered strong growth in deliveries and earnings this quarter, backed by a resilient supply chain and close customer engagement.

Europe was mixed, the UK stayed weak

In the Netherlands, revenue stood at 1,395 million euros and EBITDA at 72 million euros, helped by the restart of the Direct Sheet Plant in early August. Liquid steel production was 1.52 million tonnes and deliveries were 1.30 million tonnes. BusinessLine, quoting chief financial officer Koushik Chatterjee, said Netherlands EBITDA improved from 4 million euros in the first quarter to 72 million euros in the second, aided by favourable pricing and the plant restart.

In the United Kingdom, revenue was 411 million pounds and the company reported an EBITDA loss of 56 million pounds, with deliveries of 0.38 million tonnes. Tata Steel attributed the difficult UK environment to elevated imports and inventory build-up across parts of the value chain.

Capex, debt and the board change

The company spent about Rs 3,280 crore on capital expenditure during the quarter, taking first-half FY27 spending to Rs 6,860 crore. Projects under way include a 4.8 million-tonne-per-annum capacity expansion at Neelachal Ispat Nigam, a 0.7 million-tonne Hot Rolled Pickling and Galvanising Line, and a 300,000-tonne tinplate expansion.

Net debt stood at Rs 91,423 crore. BusinessLine reported gross debt increased to Rs 1.02 lakh crore, against Rs 97,985 crore in the June quarter, with cash and cash equivalents of Rs 10,301 crore and group liquidity of Rs 40,076 crore.

Separately, Noel Naval Tata will retire as a non-executive, non-independent director and vice chairman of the board at the close of business on November 11, 2026. BusinessLine said he has been associated with the company since March 2022. For the first half of FY27, consolidated revenue was Rs 1,26,231 crore and EBITDA was Rs 20,035 crore, with a margin of around 16%. Tata Steel shares had ended Friday's session on the BSE at Rs 186, up 2.20% from the previous close of Rs 182, in coverage published before the results were announced on Saturday.
